must_fix.title: Raw-output guard flags new nw worker writes
must_fix.detail: tests/test_rich_output_guard.py::test_no_unlisted_raw_writes (reproduced on rerun) fails on 7 raw writes (click.echo / print) in the new modules: agentic/cli_worker.py worker_info (l.37, plain-text info), worker_have (l.51, one sha per line), worker_gc (l.68, JSON summary); agentic/worker.py gate_job (l.429 stderr cleanup warning), _fail (l.436, l.446 stderr diagnostics), ssh_command (l.666, `refused: <reason>` on stderr). These are machine/protocol output paths (stdout is the frame protocol; ssh-command's stderr is the forced-command contract), so they must stay raw rather than go through rich. Fix: add entries to the ALLOWED dict at the top of tests/test_rich_output_guard.py, keyed (path relative to src/nightwright, function name) -> reason. Check the existing keys' format (e.g. ('cli.py','projects_list_cmd')) and use the rel path as the test computes it: ('agentic/cli_worker.py','worker_info'), ('agentic/cli_worker.py','worker_have'), ('agentic/cli_worker.py','worker_gc'), ('agentic/worker.py','gate_job'), ('agentic/worker.py','_fail'), ('agentic/worker.py','ssh_command'). Give each a reason such as 'machine output: worker protocol / plain stdout for ssh callers' or 'stderr diagnostic after the frame stream closed; no rich on a protocol channel'. Keep every entry real, because test_allowlist_has_no_stale_entries fails on entries that match no raw write, so do not add names that are not flagged (for example the func name for l.436 and l.446 is _fail, a nested function name as reported in the failure).
